one_liner: EcoWay Pursuit wants a reliable fix for double-booked charging bays and safer, retryable payouts before its November 30 board demo.
background: EcoWay Pursuit is a marketplace for booking EV charging bays at private sites, built as a Rails monolith on PostgreSQL with Sidekiq and a React Native app. Four engineers maintain it, and site owners are paid through Stripe Connect.
goals: Choose a way to make double bookings impossible, and ship it before November 30.
Decide how payouts should run instead of one fragile nightly batch.
Make webhook handling and payouts safe to retry without paying anyone twice.
key_facts: About 40,000 bookings per month, peaking on Friday afternoons.
Roughly 0.3% of peak-hour bookings are double-booked.
The booking check reads existing bookings, then inserts if the slot looks free.
Payouts to 180 site owners run as one nightly batch, which failed fully or partly four times in two months.
Stripe webhooks are processed inline in a Rails controller.
Board demo on November 30; no plan to split the monolith this year.
questions: Database constraints, row locks, or something else to stop double bookings?
Per-booking transfers or a separate payout service instead of the nightly batch?
How to make webhooks and payouts safe to retry?
gaps: Whether anyone has actually been paid twice after manual re-runs is unknown.
No numbers on peak requests per second or database load.
No detail on how bookings and slots are modelled in the schema.
Unclear whether payouts currently use Stripe idempotency keys or any record of what was paid.

agenda.topic: Walk through the booking flow and the race between check and insert
Options to prevent double bookings, and a plan to ship one before November 30
Payout design: batch vs per-booking transfers, and auditing past runs
Priorities for the next four weeks
